Commentary.Commentary: India's bowlers were made to toil really hard on a very docile and slow surface. Turn on offer was very slow too, neutralizing India's spin trio. Jadeja still probed a bit but Ashwin and Mishra weren't able to penetrate with the leggie being particularly erratic. It's a quite flat pitch but England have runs on the board. The Indian innings is coming up shortly.

England have finally been bowled out. A fab batting effort from the visitors after opting to bat. Ali's gritty century led the charge yesterday with good support from Root. Ashwin and Jadeja were probing with their lines and lengths while Ishant and Umesh managed to hurry the batsmen. India will want to wrap up the final three wickets as quickly as possible. England on the other hand, will want the tail to dig in and at least get them past the psychological 400-run mark. Join us in a short while for the second session.

29 overs, 68 runs, 3 wickets - India have fought back well to win this morning session. The hosts started with great discipline and were rewarded instantly. Stokes fell in the first over of the day while Buttler too didn't last long. The short ball ploy once again got rid of Ali to end the southpaw's marathon knock. Ishant gets rewarded for his impeccable line and England have again lost their batsmen in quick succession.
Pitched outside off, Ali guides it towards third man for a single.
Outside off, Buttler tries to defend it but the ball gets an inside edge onto his pads. They run a quick single as the ball tickles away towards the point region.
Short again, Moeen pulls it in an unorthodox manner but the ball falls short of the fielder at square leg for a single.

Buttler covers the line and blocks it well.

No bat involved but ball tracking shows the impact outside off which settles the issue. Would have only clipped off stump anyway. The on-field call will stay. Needless gamble from India this. They need to use DRS better.

IN THE AIR! Another short one, Moeen Ali pulls it and the ball flies of the top edge towards fine leg for a single. The ball fell just short of the fine leg fielder. Amit Mishra on fine leg was really slow there.
Dug in short, Ali ducks under that bumper.
Pitched outside off, the ball finds the inside edge and thuds into his pads.
Buttler shuffles across and guides the ball towards fine leg for a couple.
Moeen Ali camps back and cuts it towards point for a single.
Ali covers his stumps and lets that ball through.

Ashwin gets a wicket in the first over of the day. He seems to have an advantage over Stokes just like Jadeja has an advantage over Cook.
Pitched up, Moeen Ali leans forward to drive it to long off for a single.
Stokes comes down the track and drives it towards long off for a single.
Anging into the stumps, Stokes camps back and punches it towards point.
Tossed up outside off, Moeen Ali drives through covers for a single.
Players are out in the middle. MOEEN ALI and BEN STOKES will continue their partnership. ASHWIN will start the proceedings with the ball for India.

Sunil Gavaskar reckons its a very beautiful batting surface. Some foot marks here and there but that should not be a big problem. He also adds that if Jadeja and Ashwin bowl up then they will start troubling the batsmen. Also adds that they will concede an odd boundary in the process of earning wickets. He appreciates the batting of Moeen Ali whose grit on the pitch is commendable and also reckons that 400 will not be enough on this batting friendly wicket.

Mooen Ali batted really superbly as he got to his hundred and kept on going till the end of the day. Bairstow was unlucky to get out a run before his half century. Ishant bowled really well and he was the pick of the Indian bowlers. The spin trio could not cause much damage yesterday but they will love to do the talking with the ball today. Can England impose a big total on the board or will they stutter like they have always done in this series so far? Join us in a while as the action isn't far away.

Welcome one and all to the second day of the final Test match between India and England. The visitors had an exciting day with the bat yesterday despite losing their openers cheaply early on. Root and Moeen batted really well in the initial phase where they were seen struggling for 21-2 in the first hour of the play.
...DAY 2, SESSION 1...

Jadeja was the pick of the bowlers with a 3-fer on a track that slowed down as the day progressed. There was spin but the batsmen had time to adjust due to the slowness of the surface. It didn't deter the left-arm spinner as he bowled with great control, outbowling his spin partners. England will want to keep consolidating and aim for a total of at least 400 from here. India will hope to make early inroads tomorrow. Join us at 0930 IST for the second day's play. Till then, it's goodbye from us. Cheers!

A good day for England and they needed this after the battering in Mumbai. The visitors won another good toss and ensured that their batsmen made it count. Ali's gritty century (after a reprieve on 0) was the highlight of the day while Root too played a fluent knock although he was unlucky to miss the three-figure mark. The duo's efforts along with a neat little knock from Bairstow allowed England to go to stumps on a happy note despite the wicketkeeper batsman falling late in the day.
Very full and outside off, Ben Stokes jams it out towards the off side. They wait for the umpires to make a call and there comes the bails. IT IS STUMPS ON DAY 1!

Welcome back for the final session. Which side will take the day's honors? We shall find out in the coming couple of hours. The players and umpires are out there in the middle. UMESH YADAV to begin proceedings after tea.
.....DAY 1, SESSION 3....

India's bowlers were a bit erratic. Rather, they were unsettled by some positive batting from the visitors. Jadeja was the impressive bowler in the session as he continued to probe away while Mishra struggled with his radar. It will be imperative for England not to gift away the platform that has been provided by the Root-Ali stand. India are surely sensing an opening though. Join us in a while for the final session.

Good session for England. Root and Ali batted with great intent after lunch and seized the initiative by scoring freely. The former looked set for a century but was dismissed in slightly debatable circumstances. He got out in the 80s for the umpteenth time in Tests. Ali has looked quite solid after a struggle in the morning session and has the in-form Bairstow for company.

India's bowlers were very disciplined, giving very little away. They stuck to the basics and created pressure on the England batsmen. The surface has started to turn already and this certainly isn't good a omen for the visitors. They will need to put a decent first innings total to compete in this game. Partnerships are key for England and they will hope the current one continues longer. India know that wickets can come in clumps on this pitch. Join us in a while for the next session.

An even session for both sides although India would marginally be the happier side at the break after losing the toss. England started disastrously after opting to bat as both openers departed cheaply. Jennings was beautifully set up by Ishant while Jadeja once again derailed Cook. Pitched outside off, left alone.
Angling into the stumps, Jennings gets an inside edge to his pads. A mild appeal is denied by the umpire.
Bowling on the stumps, Jennings gets in line of the ball to defend it.
Wide! Very wide outside off, the umpire has called that a wide.
Cook has pushed that one to the cover region for a single.
Pitched up on the stmps, Cook finds a leading edge which goes towards the cover region for a couple. Cook reaches to 11,000 Test runs.
The players are out in the middle. COOK and JENNINGS come out to bat. UMESH YADAV has taken the new ball.
Both teams and officials are out in the middle for their respective National Anthems. All the players are wearing a black arm band to pay homage to the victims of the cyclone in Chennai.

Kohli wasn't asked about the changes but as has been the norm in all the games under his leadership, it isn't an unchanged XI for India. Jayant Yadav and Bhuvneshwar Kumar make way for Amit Mishra and Ishant Sharma.

VIRAT KOHLI isn't bothered about losing the toss as he feels the batting side would be under pressure. Reasons that the dampness in the track should aid their seamers. Maintains that there is no complacency in the side and states that they are keen to finish on a high. Lauds the Chennai crowd for their knowledge and feels that having two local boys (Ashwin and Vijay) will help.

ALASTAIR COOK says that they will bat first. Feels it is a reasonably good surface. Feels that it's strange not to have a net practice heading into this game but also adds that playing continuous cricket makes it a non factor. Hopes that his side is mentally strong to salvage some pride. Reveals that there are two changes - Dawson makes his debut while Broad is back in. Anderson and Woakes miss out.
Time for the toss. Kohli to spin the coin. Heads is the call from Cook, it is a head. The visiting skipper calls it right for the fourth time in the series. ENGLAND WIN THE TOSS AND OPT TO BAT.
